review.title: The Empty Barn
review.headline: Six farmers egged an innocent Hawk, then one Eagle visit banked 65 points.
review.summary: Round 1 had no Meowfia at all. Alex misread a Turkey egg as a Tit hit, and the table piled onto Finley, the honest Hawk. Every thrown card was lost. In round 2, five players happened to visit the Meowfia Sphinx Casey. Finley's Eagle got four eggs and a full visitor list, so Casey was an easy catch, and Finley won by 50 points.

rounds.recap: Everyone was Farm. Alex Tit guessed that Blair was the Hawk and got an egg, but the egg came from Blair's Turkey. Alex then called Finley's true Hawk claim a lie. Finley was the only player nobody could confirm, so he got 24 cards thrown at him. Nobody considered that there might be no Meowfia, and every thrown card was lost.

Blair, Drew, Ellis, Finley and the Meowfia Floofer Alex all visited Casey, the Sphinx. Finley's Eagle reported all four visitors, and two of them confirmed it. Casey claimed Tit, which clashed with Drew's claim, and deflected badly. All four Farm players threw at Casey and won. Alex never said a word and slipped through.

highlights.text: Finley warned, "If I'm eggsecuted and I'm Farm, Meowfia win," and he was right, because there were no Meowfia, but nobody listened.
Alex's confident 'I know Blair is the Hawk' started the pile-on, and it rested entirely on a Turkey egg.
Five of six players visited Casey on the same night, which turned Finley's Eagle into a 4-egg jackpot and a public map of the night.
Blair learned that Casey was the Sphinx and never said so, but still credited 'Casey's Sphinx reveal' in the survey.

confusions.what: Assumed his egg came from a correct Tit guess. It came from Blair's Turkey, and that led him to call Blair the Hawk and Finley a liar.
Said Casey's Eagle had visited him, but Casey had clearly said she visited Drew.
Said 'I said it earlier: Kookaburra', but Ellis had never claimed a role before that.
Called Casey's Drew visit 'shaky' even though Drew's and Casey's egg reports matched exactly.
Said 'I confirmed twice' and quoted a Tit claim from his 'first message', but Drew had not spoken before. That line was never said.
Said 'Confirmed again', but it was Ellis's first confirmation.
Used Ellis's round 1 role as evidence, even though roles are re-dealt every round.
Never told the table his Kookaburra result (Casey is the Sphinx), but later acted as if the reveal had decided the round.
Believed he was 'hiding as a Pigeon' but never claimed any role at the table.

problems: No-Meowfia rounds happen about 9% of the time ((2/3)^6), and they wiped out round 1 completely. Nobody even considered the possibility, so the game came down to one round. Consider giving a small hint, or letting an all-Farm table win if the vote is spread out.

The Eagle's egg gain is far too strong when visits pile up. Four visitors gave 4 eggs, and those eggs were worth 65 banked points, 50 more than second place. Consider capping the Eagle at 1-2 eggs, or making the eggs 1-point cards.

Possible engine or report bug. The log says 'Casey (Sphinx) is hugged: no effect at tier 50', and Casey's dawn report shows none of the Sphinx information (the Farm roles in play, or who the Eagle is). Yet Casey threw at Finley as a 'known Farm'. Check whether a hug blocks the Sphinx, and make the report show what was learned.

Dawn reports don't say where an egg came from, so a Tit hit and a Turkey egg look identical. That caused the most costly mistake of the game. Either say where Tit eggs come from, or make the Tit's reward something other than an egg.

Players often remember lines they wrote but lost the bid on (Drew and Ellis in both rounds). Give each player the actual transcript, or a 'you did not speak' reminder. Separately: the Floofer's hug landed on its own teammate, its passive never triggered, and Mouser, Wink, House Cat and Pigeon never came up.
